catalog.title: Evaluate a probe
catalog.mac: Research methods: Author request, review inputs, then open execution and evidence. Both CLIs use science interview/draft/publish and the same managed engine.
outputs: Immutable run with pinned inputs, provenance, and inspectable probe evidence.
catalog.restriction: Bounded binary probe workflow. Predictive accuracy is not causal evidence or calibrated probability. Capture uses the Python engine; fitting and evaluation use shared CPU owners. Legacy readers are preserved.

actions.authorityReason: Inspect staged scientific inputs and execution resources without execution or authorship.
Execute a reviewed scientific operation and retain its scientific output type.

access.restriction: Calls the existing route with its existing service role and scientific gates. Request path parameters, query and body remain explicit; this adapter does not change execution topology or retry mutations.

interview.title: Evaluate a probe
interview.purpose: Measure a pinned probe on separately chosen activations. Preserve the trained instrument and save a new report.

fields.label: Saved probe
fields.help: Choose trained.probe.json. Existing legacy readers remain usable in their original paths; this evaluator needs the portable v1 input binding.

fields.label: Evaluation activations
fields.help: Choose finalTest-activations.json for a final assessment, or another matching dataset for exploration. Same model, rendering, site, and coordinates are required.

fields.label: Purpose of this evaluation
fields.help: finalTest or exploratory. Known training/selection overlap is reported prominently without blocking exploration. Different hashes alone do not prove independence.

interview.claimBoundary: An activation classifier predicts the supplied labels in this population. It does not establish that the model uses the predicted feature causally.
questions: What do the labels mean, and which related examples belong in one group?
Which data are for fitting, choosing settings, and final assessment?
